issues.claim: J149's over form lets a gate stand under an aqueduct's arch that clears it: law 1 (5) (base l. 2722-2723) bars a gate's footprint in a strip 'but in an aqueduct's crossing law 1 (2) reads over whose every span over it clears its top', law 1 (6) (l. 2724-2725) admits a fixed place there likewise and an aqueduct has no zone (l. 2633); law 2 (a) and law 3's key (1) (l. 2843) keep a value the op set where lawful and move what it places to the nearest place the laws admit. W13 (l. 3341), Strips, zones and nearest points (l. 3002-3003), the way-and-channel table's row (b) (l. 2912), T110-2 (4) (l. 19378-19381: 'the placed gate moved along the trace to the nearest place §2.7's laws admit it (... clear of the strip, or under an aqueduct's arch that clears it)') and T-V7-48 (V07 l. 3708: 'moved along the palisade to the nearest lawful point') were conformed. §7.1's outcome table, 'the one home of every ... bend cause of a dry run' (l. 11265), was not: its bend.wall.raisedCrossing row (l. 11323) takes 'a placeGate or a gate's slid crossing inside its under-deck strip' and gives 'a slid gate moved back along the trace to the strip's edge its grip came from and a placeGate's gate to the nearer edge', and keeps 'a fixed place it lays ... out of the fixed-place zone (law 1 (6))', a zone an aqueduct lacks; its bend.raised.underSpan row (l. 11325) bends a hand way 'crossing an enceinte's trace inside that strip ... to the nearest clear of the under-deck strip', copied by V09 l. 2105 ('{name} crosses {wall} at a gate clear of {way}'). A gate placed under a clearing arch, a placed or slid gate with a clearing arch nearer than the strip's edge, and a hand road crossing a wall under a clearing arch square to the deck are bent to the strip's edge by §7.1 and kept or stopped at the nearer lawful place by the laws: a lawful declaration bent or a nearer lawful place passed, against item 101 R2 (Part P's PRB7H-LCK-03 pattern: not a valid choice), failing T110-2 (4)'s and T-V7-48's placed-gate clauses, and for the road no bar runs the case (T-V9-52, T110-2 (5) l. 19446-19448 run road decks); a water gate a hand stretch lays under an aqueduct arch that does not clear it has no move from §7.1's words.
issues.required_change: 1. §7.1's bend.wall.raisedCrossing row (l. 11323): cause 'or a `placeGate` or a gate's slid crossing inside its under-deck strip' -> 'or a `placeGate` or a gate's slid crossing where §2.7's laws bar a gate there (law 1 (5): inside a road deck's under-deck strip, or inside an aqueduct's unless its arches there clear the gate and the wall and its way passes the strip by §4.3's crossing rule)'; outcome 'a fixed place it lays kept out of the fixed-place zone (law 1 (6))' -> 'a fixed place it lays placed where law 1 (6) admits it (out of a road deck's fixed-place zone, and out of an aqueduct's strip but under arches that clear it and the wall)'; and 'a slid gate moved back along the trace to the strip's edge its grip came from and a `placeGate`'s gate to the nearer edge' -> 'a placed or slid gate moved along the trace to the nearest point at which §2.7's laws admit its footprint (law 1 (5): clear of the strip, or under an aqueduct's arch that clears it and the wall) — a `placeGate`'s gate to the nearer such point, a slid one back to the first such point on the side its grip came from'. 2. §7.1's bend.raised.underSpan row (l. 11325): 'or crossing an enceinte's trace inside that strip' -> 'or crossing an enceinte's trace where §2.7's laws bar its gate there (law 1 (5): inside a road deck's under-deck strip, or inside an aqueduct's unless its arches there clear the gate and the wall and the way passes the strip by §4.3's crossing rule)'; and 'its crossing of a trace to the nearest clear of the under-deck strip' -> 'its crossing of a trace to the nearest at which those laws admit its gate'. 3. END at V09 (one fix with VF7-RDR-08): §4.9's bend.raised.underSpan source cell (V09 l. 2105) takes item 2's trigger, and its wall form '"{name} crosses {wall} at a gate clear of {way}, {m} m off your line."' -> '"{name} crosses {wall} where a gate can stand, {m} m off your line."'; bend.wall.raisedCrossing's gate form (V09 l. 2104) '"No gate can stand beneath {way}, so it moves {m} m along {wall}."' -> '"No gate can stand there beneath {way}, so it moves {m} m along {wall}."'. 4. END at scope, T110-2 (5) (l. 19446-19448): after 'a hand road drawn across one where a wall runs beneath it, crossing the trace under the deck — moved along the deck to cross the trace clear of the under-deck strip at a gate (`bend.raised.underSpan`)' add '; a hand road drawn across a wall under a standing aqueduct's arch that clears the gate and the wall, square to the deck — its gate made there, no bend — and, on a second run where that arch does not clear the gate, moved along the deck to the nearest crossing at which §2.7's laws admit its gate (§2.7's laws, law 1 (5), law 2 (a), law 3)'.

issues.claim: Law 1 (2) (base l. 2703-2711) makes a crossing over only 'where its channel there lies above the wall's top — no standing support in the band there and every span above the band clearing the wall's top', merged only where the channel lies within the wall's height, and 'a crossing that fits neither form is unlawful' — the restoration Part P's pass 6 flagged as an OWNER-RULE CLASH (PRB7F-GEN-03: pass 5's 'every crossing lawful whatever the level' against J149). Over the band (l. 3010-3024: 'every span over the band clearing the wall's top ... a declared one bent to the nearest course that can, else refused'), the bent group's lawful crossing (l. 3177-3179), T110-2 (4) (l. 19363-19366: a hand drawWall through a support 'where its channel runs above the wall's top, bent along the deck to cross under the nearest span that clears the wall') and T-V9-52 carry it. Three hand texts keep pass 5's reading: §7.1's bend.wall.raisedCrossing row (l. 11323: 'an aqueduct's deck line crossed once anywhere, in the form its level there gives'); §7.1 Raised ways (l. 11131-11135: 'its course bent clear only of a gate, postern, tower or fixed place its arches would not clear'); V09 §4.20.2 (4) (V09 l. 3019-3023: 'over ... its supports off the band and its spans clearing the wall, else merged into it ..., its course bent clear only of ...'). For a hand aqueduct whose channel at the wall runs above the wall's top by less than the deck's depth (span.deckDepthCm 150, V11 l. 3980), so its span over the band does not clear the wall, and for a hand wall drawn through such an aqueduct's support: the laws bend the course (else refuse) and the wall stroke; the hand texts bend neither, or read the crossing merged with a high channel — a crossing in neither of J149's forms (law 1 (2) broken, §5.3's law-1 row failing the edit with no outcome §7.1 gives) or a refusal where a lawful bend exists (item 101 R2). T110-2 (4) fails such a build on the wall stroke; no bar runs the aqueduct stroke's case (T110-2 (1), l. 19278-19283, bends for a tower and refuses for supports only). The hand member of VF7-GEN-01's class.
issues.required_change: 1. §7.1's bend.wall.raisedCrossing row (l. 11323): '(an aqueduct's deck line crossed once anywhere, in the form its level there gives, law 1 (2);' -> '(an aqueduct's deck line crossed once in the form its level there gives — over where its channel runs above the wall's top, under a span that clears it and never through a standing support; merged where it runs within the wall's height — law 1 (2);'. 2. §7.1 Raised ways (l. 11133-11135): 'never a gate, its course bent clear only of a gate, postern, tower or fixed place its arches would not clear (item 363; §2.7's laws, law 1 (2), (5), (6); law 2 (a);' -> 'never a gate, a course that cannot cross so — an over crossing whose span over the band would not clear the wall's top, a gate, postern, tower or fixed place its arches would not clear — bent to the nearest course that can, else refused (item 363; §2.7's laws, law 1 (2), (5), (6); law 2 (a), (c);'. 3. END at V09, §4.20.2 (4) (V09 l. 3019-3023): 'over it on one of its arches where its channel there runs above the wall's top, its supports off the band and its spans clearing the wall, else merged into it, the wall built up round its arch or pier and the water passing through —, never a gate, its course bent clear only of a gate, postern, tower or fixed place its arches would not clear (§2.7's laws, law 1 (2), (5), (6), (10), law 2 (a);' -> 'over it on one of its arches where its channel there runs above the wall's top, its supports off the band and its spans clearing the wall, merged into it where its channel runs within the wall's height, the wall built up round its arch or pier and the water passing through —, never a gate, a course that cannot cross so bent to the nearest course that can, else refused (§2.7's laws, law 1 (2), (5), (6), (10), law 2 (a), (c);'. 4. END at scope, T110-2 (1) (l. 19278-19280): after 'its course bent clear of a tower whose top its arches would not clear (§2.7's laws, law 1 (5), law 2 (a)), with `bend.wall.aqueductArch`' add '— and one whose channel at the wall runs above the wall's top by less than the deck's depth, so that its span over the band would not clear it: its course bent to the nearest crossing whose span clears the wall's top, with `bend.wall.aqueductArch`, else refused `refuse.raised.meeting` (§2.7's laws, law 1 (2), law 2 (a), (c)) —'.

issues.claim: VPC-r6-03 found that the run a carve or a moved river re-traces is refused at, or cuts, a standing raised way its new strips meet (§4.11 Other crossings, and '§7.3 (b) 3 ... says the same for S1's water operator (a moved river)'). The carve is fixed: §4.11 (base l. 8946-8949) excepts 'a raised way, whose deck passes over the run' from the cut fate and makes it no conflict. §7.3 (b) 3 took only the conflict clause (E-D5, l. 11681-11684); its cut list for the moved river still reads 'By F-REDERIVE's way rung (§5.2) it cuts every other way the new channel ⊕ bank setback meets, and every way but a kept way at a gate that the new strips will meet' (l. 11675-11676), no raised-way exception. Row W2's last column (l. 3330) sends both re-traces to the carve's rule ('a carve's or a moved river's re-trace by §4.11 Other crossings'); beneath writes nothing of the raised way; law 2 (b) moves 'Never ... a Tier-2 structure's line, band, supports, spans or ends' (l. 2820); J148's Tier 2 (the owner's choice: the newer bends locally); the support step (6): 'only an op that names it changes it' (l. 2569). A hand moved river (moveCourseKnot, a hand shiftCourse) whose re-traced run's new strips meet a standing raised way keeps it by §4.11, W2 and the laws and cuts it by §7.3 (b) 3 — the older Tier-2 structure cut for the newer run, against J148. No bar runs the case: T110-2 (5) (l. 19449-19455) runs a carve, T110-2 (4)'s epoch shiftCourse (l. 19435-19440) asserts the viaduct unchanged only on its waiting run.
issues.required_change: §7.3 (b) 3 (l. 11675-11676): 'and every way but a kept way at a gate that the new strips will meet,' -> 'and every way that the new strips will meet but a kept way at a gate and a standing raised way, whose deck passes over the run and which the re-traced run meets by §2.7's laws (law 2 (a); its worked example the crossing table's row W2; §4.11 *Other crossings*),'. (no move, no distance; beyond a foot the wall does not run beneath the deck), the merged, gate, keep-clear (along beneath, one side, ending under it) and fixed-place forms.
